MEETING TRANSCRIPT
------------------
Camille: DevCon planning, eight weeks out, let's lock the big rocks. Venue first. The convention center finally sent the revised quote: 18,000 for the main hall plus two breakout rooms, catering separate. That's within budget.

Diego: That's 4k under what we modeled, nice.

Camille: I want it signed before they change their minds. Diego, get the contract through legal review and signed by end of next week, and confirm the AV package includes recording in all three rooms, last year we lost the breakout talks because recording was main-hall only.

Diego: Contract, legal, signature, and AV recording in writing for all three rooms. Got it.

Camille: Speakers. We have six confirmed, we need nine. Bo, where are the other three?

Bo: Two maybes, one decline. My plan: I'll send final follow-ups to the two maybes with a decision deadline of Friday, and I have a backup list of five names if either falls through. Worst case I fill the third slot from the backup list. Either way I'll have the lineup locked in two weeks so we can print the agenda.

Camille: Locked lineup in two weeks, that's the commitment. And the keynote abstract, we still don't have it.

Bo: I'll chase Dr. Osei for the keynote abstract this week, we need it for the website and the printed program.

Camille: Marketing. Registration is at 340 against a target of 600.

Diego: Historically the surge comes after the agenda goes live, but we shouldn't just wait. I'll run the email campaign in three waves: agenda announcement when Bo locks the lineup, early-bird deadline reminder two weeks before the price change, and a final-week push. I'll draft all three this month, and the first wave goes out the day the agenda is live.

Camille: Good. And the website needs the speaker pages before wave one, obviously. Bo, once the lineup locks, hand the bios and headshots straight to Diego for the landing page update, same day, don't sit on them.

Bo: Same-day handoff, understood.

Camille: Swag. Last year we ran out of the good stuff in two hours.

Diego: Order's ready to place: 800 shirts across sizes, 500 notebooks, 1,000 stickers, comes to about 9,200 with the rush buffer. I just need your sign-off on the design proofs, they're in the shared drive.

Camille: I'll review the proofs today, and once I approve, you place the order this week, lead time was six weeks last year, we're already cutting it close.

Diego: The moment you approve, it's ordered.

Camille: That's everything on my list. Venue, speakers, keynote abstract, email waves, speaker pages, swag. Next check-in same time in two weeks, with the lineup locked and the contract signed, please.
